title: ChatGPT-Assisted Lesson Planning for Children’s STEAM Arts Education: An Experimental Study on Benefits, Challenges, Methods, and a Prompt Framework
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether and how generative AI, specifically ChatGPT, can improve lesson planning quality for children’s STEAM arts education. The authors focus on a practical problem faced by art teachers: lesson planning is time-consuming, resource-intensive, and often constrained by difficulty finding high-quality, age-appropriate, and interdisciplinary materials. The study asks what benefits and challenges arise when teachers use ChatGPT for lesson planning, how teachers can use it effectively, and what prompting approach produces better lesson plan content.

The intervention studied is ChatGPT-assisted lesson planning, compared against traditional teacher-generated planning. Teachers first created lesson plans in their usual way and then produced AI-assisted plans using GPT-4o and a structured prompt framework. The lesson theme centered on color art for primary-age children (approximately 6–12 years old), with a focus on STEAM arts instruction. A pre-study gathered teacher perceptions, then 13 art teachers created plans in Experiment 1, and 6 university professors in Experiment 2 evaluated the resulting lesson plans using a rubric adapted from the 5E model.

The study found that ChatGPT improved lesson planning efficiency and the quality of lesson plans, especially in content development, interdisciplinary integration, and resource generation. Professors scored ChatGPT-assisted plans higher than traditional plans overall, and teachers reported positive experiences and willingness to continue using the tool. At the same time, the paper identifies important limitations of ChatGPT, including weak personalization, occasional impracticality for everyday classroom use, and safety/appropriateness issues in generated content. The authors conclude that ChatGPT is best understood as a support tool for teacher-AI collaboration rather than a replacement for teachers, and they propose a prompt framework to improve future use in arts lesson planning.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI chatbot based on GPT-family large language models, used for text generation, iteration, and assistance with content creation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by teachers to collaboratively generate and refine lesson plans for children's STEAM arts education, with GPT-4o used as the specific model/account in the experiment and a prompt framework provided to guide prompting.

findings.finding_summary: In the experimental comparison of 25 lesson plans (12 traditional, 13 ChatGPT-assisted), professors rated ChatGPT-assisted lesson plans higher than traditional plans. The paper reports average total scores of 21.0 for ChatGPT-assisted plans versus 17.0 for traditional plans.

Teachers reported that ChatGPT improved lesson planning efficiency, including faster topic selection, faster generation of instructional content, and reduced planning time. Reported average scores were 3.7 for topic selection speed, 3.8 for rapid generation of high-quality instructional content, and 4.2 for reduced lesson planning time.
findings.measure: Teacher survey on lesson planning efficiency

findings.finding_summary: Teachers generally agreed that ChatGPT improved lesson planning quality. The sub-items 'The content generated by ChatGPT is accurate' and 'The lesson plan generated by ChatGPT meets my requirements' received average scores of 4.0 and 3.9, respectively.
findings.measure: Teacher survey on lesson planning content quality and fit to requirements

findings.finding_summary: For interdisciplinary integration, 61% of respondents rated ChatGPT at 4 or above, indicating that it supported cross-disciplinary lesson planning. The paper describes this as evidence of robust support for multidisciplinary integration in STEAM lesson design.

Teachers were neutral about ChatGPT's role in fostering innovation. The paper states that ChatGPT was more useful as a source of inspiration than as a generator of entirely novel content, and that true innovation still depended on human observation and creativity.

Overall satisfaction with ChatGPT for lesson planning was positive, with an average satisfaction score of 3.9 and a future-use score of 4.1 among 13 teachers. The authors interpret this as indicating strong willingness to continue using the tool for lesson planning.
findings.measure: Teacher satisfaction and intention for future use

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods experimental study with a small convenience sample (13 teachers, 6 professors). It includes a comparative evaluation of lesson plans, but the evidence is not a randomized controlled trial and effect sizes/confidence intervals are not reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports a meaningful improvement in professor-rated lesson plan quality (21.0 vs 17.0) and positive efficiency ratings, suggesting practical benefit. However, the magnitude is not quantified with an effect size and the study is small and context-specific, so overall impact remains somewhat unclear.
